title: Is my shop as busy as my graph says? Node.js cluster metrics, counted two ways
description: otel-cluster-metrics against the stock exporter, same app, same traffic.

options.content:
## Is my shop as busy as my graph says?
The usual OpenTelemetry setup kept showing my shop way more visitors than it really got. So I run the same made-up shop twice and send the same visitors to both. Each one runs as four copies of the same Node.js app, and every four minutes one copy gets swapped out (the faint violet lines).

**Orange** is the usual setup. **Blue** is my package, [otel-cluster-metrics](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics). **Green** is what the visitors actually got back, counted by the program sending them, which has no OpenTelemetry code in it.

panels.title: Usual setup vs what visitors got
panels.description: The usual setup's count divided by the answers the visitors actually got back from that shop, over the last hour. 1× would mean it counts right.

panels.title: Visitors a second, counted three ways
panels.description: Orange jumps because Prometheus reads a different copy each time and thinks the count started over. Blue and green sit on top of each other. The violet lines mark a new copy of the app starting.

targets.expr: count by (worker) (label_replace((max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"}) unless max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)) and on () count(max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)), "worker", "$1", "cluster_worker_id", "([0-9]+):.*"))

panels.title: My package vs what visitors got
panels.description: My package's count divided by the answers the visitors got back, over the last hour. If a copy is killed without warning, up to about 10 seconds of counts can be lost, so it can sit a little under 1×.

panels.title: Visitors the usual setup made up, last 24 hours
panels.description: How many more visitors the usual setup counted than the visitors actually got back, over the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Count resets, last hour
panels.description: How often a count went down, which Prometheus reads as a restart. Mine saves its totals to a file, so its count does not go down when the main program restarts.

panels.title: Copies the graph can see (the shop runs four)
panels.description: Both shops run four copies. Each time mine reports, the report has all of them. Each scrape of the usual setup only shows the copy that happened to answer.

options.content:
The green line's check is one command you can run on your own app. It sends requests, reads your app's counter and tells you how far the graph is off:

`npx @adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics check --target http://127.0.0.1:3000/ --metrics http://127.0.0.1:9464/metrics --counter requests_total`

On the test app in the repo, the usual setup counted **0.26×** what the app really answered. My package counted **1.00×**. [How to use it](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics#check-your-request-graph)

panels.title: The raw counter, and what each setup has counted
Requests counter as Prometheus sees it
panels.description: The raw running count, next to the responses the visitors got back (green). Restart both main programs with `docker compose restart shop-api shop-api-stock`. Mine saves its totals to a file, so blue carries on next to green. The usual setup shows one copy's count per scrape, so it jumps and drops, and starts again from zero after a restart. Violet markers infer new copies from successive samples.

targets.expr: count by (worker) (label_replace((max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"}) unless max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)) and on () count(max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)), "worker", "$1", "cluster_worker_id", "([0-9]+):.*"))

panels.title: Requests counted, whole shop
panels.description: Every request my package has counted since this copy of the demo started. It carries on across a main program restart because the totals are saved to a file. A hard kill can lose increments recorded after the last snapshot.

panels.title: Requests counted, usual setup (one worker only)
panels.description: Not the shop's total: only the count kept by whichever worker answered the last scrape. Right after that worker is swapped it reads as low as 1.

panels.title: p95 request latency
panels.description: Merged histograms add counts, sums and buckets across workers. The usual setup's line is one worker's sample.

panels.title: Requests per second by route
panels.description: Monotonic sums: one latest snapshot per worker, retired workers' totals kept.

panels.title: Checkout errors per minute
panels.description: About 3% of checkouts fail on purpose.

panels.title: In-flight requests and email queue, whole cluster
panels.description: Non-monotonic sums add current worker values and drop exited workers. Each checkout queues confirmation emails, and the queue gauge is summed across live workers.

panels.title: V8 heap per worker
panels.description: Heap gauges use a separate series for each worker and boot. A line ends when its worker is retired and a new one starts with the next ID.

panels.title: Worker processes seen, 24h
panels.description: Each boot gets its own ID, so this counts restarts too.

panels.title: Seconds since my package's last count
panels.description: Time since the newest sample of the merged count. An incomplete round gives no count at all, a 503 for a scrape or nothing sent for an OTLP push, so a gap here is a missed round, never a partial count.

panels.title: Requests in the last hour, merged
Client transport failures, last hour
panels.description: Failed or timed-out requests per target. HTTP 500 responses count as received responses and are not transport failures. A mismatch between server and client counters is not solely evidence of telemetry loss.

options.content:
**shop-api** uses [otel-cluster-metrics](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics). **shop-api-stock** runs a stock OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter in each worker on one shared port. The independent **load** process counts attempts, received responses, transport failures and in-flight requests for each target at `/metrics`.

Prometheus scrapes all three every 15 seconds. The default demo replaces the oldest worker every four minutes, choosing SIGKILL with 20% probability and SIGTERM otherwise. Violet bars show new worker IDs, not exit signals. The primary logs each actual exit signal. A hard kill can lose the last worker snapshot window, normally up to 10 seconds. shop-api keeps its totals in a file (`STATE_FILE`), so they survive `docker compose restart shop-api shop-api-stock`. shop-api-stock starts again from zero.

Run [examples/grafana](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics/tree/main/examples/grafana) with `docker compose up`, then open Grafana on port 3000. Wait at least two scrapes for rates. The shape changes as workers age and restart. No fixed inflation factor is promised. For known-input correctness, run `npm test` and `node examples/single-task-workers.cjs` from the repository root.
